q: The Carathéodory extension theorem says that a premeasure μ₀ on an algebra 𝒜 extends to a measure on the σ-algebra σ(𝒜). The extension is unique when:
exp: Carathéodory extension is always possible, and uniqueness holds when μ₀ is σ-finite (X = ∪Xₙ with μ₀(Xₙ) < ∞). Without σ-finiteness, multiple extensions can exist.
